title: Positivist Calendar
intro: Auguste Comte's proposed calendar reorganised the year around thirteen equal months and names celebrating significant people from world history.
summary: Thirteen months of 28 days each, plus festival days. In this model, Gregorian 1789 marks Great Crisis Year 1.
origin: The philosopher Auguste Comte developed the Positivist Calendar in the nineteenth century as part of a proposed social and intellectual reform.
structure: Thirteen months each have four seven-day weeks. Special festival days complete the solar year and align with Gregorian leap years.
pattern_note: Each regular month is four weeks long. Extra festival days are not normal month days; the proposed structure differs from Gregorian months.
history: Comte named months after figures he regarded as important to humanity's intellectual and social development. The scheme was a reform proposal, not a calendar adopted by all governments.
example: Gregorian 1789 is labelled Great Crisis Year 1; Gregorian 2026 corresponds to Great Crisis Year 238 under this arithmetic year count.
limits: The provider represents Comte's proposed chronology and Gregorian leap alignment. Mathematical projections should not be treated as evidence of general civil adoption.
